title: Embedding queue compaction and kernel adaptivity to cut tail latency
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Production embeddings endpoints are seeing intermittent p99 spikes (up to 450ms) during moderate load bursts. Investigation shows queue skewing between tenants, inefficient packetization of small requests, and suboptimal kernel selection for short sequence lengths. This ticket combines a behavioral change in the ingress queue (compaction + skew detection) with runtime kernel adaptivity for short/variable-length batches to reduce tail latency without sacrificing throughput or cost.

Goals:
- Reduce embeddings endpoint p99 from ~450ms to <220ms at current 200rps mix.
- Keep median latency within 10% of baseline and maintain throughput.
- Ensure changes are behind a feature flag and can be rolled back per model or tenant.

Non-goals:
- Major changes to model quantization profiles or introducing new model variants.

Success metrics (observable via Console):
- p50 change <= +10%
- p95 <= 120ms
- p99 <= 220ms
- Error rate change <= 0.05% absolute
- No significant CPU/GPU cost regression (>5% infra cost increase)
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmark reproduces p99 <= 220ms for the standard embeddings workload (batch size distribution matching production),
Feature flag per-tenant / per-model exists and defaults to off in staging
E2E integration test validates correct behavior when queue compaction merges small packets
Canary rollout shows no increase in 5xx errors or memory pressure
Perf dashboard updated with new traces and a heatmap comparing before/after latencies
tech_notes: Ingress queue compaction: implement a sliding compaction window (100ms configurable) that batches small inbound requests into compacted micro-windows and annotates the merged packet with per-request offsets for KV caching; backpressure preserved for large requests
Skew detection: maintain per-tenancy per-shard skew counters; if skew > threshold we perform opportunistic redistribution or short-circuit kernel hints to avoid long tail waits
Kernel adaptivity: add a fast-path kernel selection for short sequences (<32 tokens) that prefers smaller launch kernels and low-occupancy kernels to avoid serialization in CUDA streams
Adaptive preemption: allow small urgent packets to preempt long-running dispatches on a best-effort basis when p99 budgets are at risk
Telemetry: emit tags for compaction_event, kernel_hint, preempted boolean, and queue_skew_percent to aid postmortems
Fallbacks: if fast-path kernels fail or produce jitter, runtime should fall back to the prior selection policy and emit an alert
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature flag and unit tests (branch: feat/eng-42177-queue-compact)
2) Run synthetic microbench in staging with recorded production arrival traces (3 days), compare p99
3) Start 5% tenant canary for tenants with medium traffic, monitor for 48 hours
4) Gradually increase to 50% and run burst fuzz tests; if stable, proceed to full rollout
5) If any regression found, toggle flag off and run quick revert PR
